findings.title: Checksum offload flags no longer force long BD; checksums silently skipped
findings.explanation: bnxt_xmit_need_long_bd() decides whether a packet is sent with a long TX BD. On bnxt hardware, only the long BD format (tx_bd_long_hi lflags) can request IP and TCP/UDP checksum offload. In bnxt_start_xmit(), the code that sets those flags runs only when long_bd is true. With RTE_MBUF_F_TX_IP_CKSUM, RTE_MBUF_F_TX_TCP_CKSUM and RTE_MBUF_F_TX_UDP_CKSUM removed from the mask, a packet that asks only for checksum offload (no VLAN, tunnel, TSO, timestamp or TruFlow CFA action) is sent with a short BD. The NIC then never computes the checksum, so packets go out with wrong or zero checksums and receivers drop them. This is the normal path for TCP/UDP apps that rely on Tx checksum offload. (The send function was outside the visible context; this relies on the known bnxt driver structure, where upstream DPDK keeps these flags here.)
findings.suggestion: Put RTE_MBUF_F_TX_TCP_CKSUM, RTE_MBUF_F_TX_UDP_CKSUM and RTE_MBUF_F_TX_IP_CKSUM back in the ol_flags mask. If short BDs are meant to support checksum offload on newer chips, gate this on a chip check and add a short-BD checksum path in bnxt_start_xmit().
